test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Though I was not happy, __I went to the reception because of the sake of my friend__.

options.text: I went to the reception for the sake of my friend
I will go to the reception for the sake of my friend
I went for the reception for the sake of my friend
I have gone to the reception because of the sake of my friend

solution:
The correct answer is **Option(1) i.e. "for the sake of my friend"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"because of the sake of"** is **redundant **and grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase is **"for the sake of"**, which means doing something for the benefit or out of consideration for someone.
 
• **"For the sake of"** is a fixed expression used to indicate the reason for doing something, especially to help or support someone.

**Therefore, the correct sentence is- "Though I was not happy, I went to the reception for the sake of my friend."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 **("I will go to the reception for the sake of my friend") changes the tense improperly, suggesting a future event rather than a past event.
 
• **Option 3 **("I went for the reception for the sake of my friend") modifies the original phrase incorrectly; "for the reception" is less specific in the context of attending an event for someone's sake.
 
• **Option 4 **("I have gone to the reception because of the sake of my friend") uses the perfect tense incorrectly for the context and repeats the original mistake.
